assertions: Lilly will purchase Master B.'s houses, including the house he lives in on the Strand: the bargain will be concluded and will not fall through.

The seller will deal favourably and honourably with Lilly, and on terms Lilly can accept: the seller's significator the Sun is placed in the 7th and received by exalted Venus near the 7th cusp, and the lord of the 7th is also lord of Lilly's 11th of hopes.

Near segment first brings difficulty and delay, not failure: Mercury, lord of Lilly's 2nd, retrograde shows his own money is not presently in hand and cannot simply be called in at once (consistent with the stated six-month lock-up).

The money will nevertheless be procured in time to pay for the purchase, on a months rather than days timescale: despite Mercury retrograde, the matter is perfected by application and translation of light, so funds are found/recalled before the payment deadline defeats the bargain.

Perfection of the purchase itself is shown by Venus applying to a trine of Saturn, lord of the 4th (the houses), and by the Moon translating light by a square out of signs of long ascension, which in Lilly's doctrine counts with the force of a trine rather than a blocking square.

The houses/title are essentially sound: Saturn, lord of the 4th, has no material debility except retrogradation and cadency, which indicate slowness and revisiting of the completion rather than a defect that ruins the purchase.
method: Classical horary astrology after William Lilly (Christian Astrology, Book II): significators of querent, seller (7th), houses (4th) and querent's money (2nd), judged by reception, application, translation of light and essential/accidental debility.
reasoning: Seller's Sun in the 7th, received by exalted Venus at the 7th cusp, and lord of 7th = lord of 11th (hopes), incline the seller to Lilly and to his hopes. Venus applying by trine to Saturn, lord of the 4th, perfects seller-to-houses; the Moon's translating square from signs of long ascension operates as a trine, carrying the matter through an apparent difficulty. Mercury lord of the 2nd retrograde and Saturn retrograde/cadent give the only contrary testimony — delay and difficulty in calling in money and in completing — not denial, since Saturn is otherwise without material debility. Hence a two-stage judgement: near-stage financial delay, far-stage purchase completed and paid for in time.
summary: Yes — Lilly shall buy Master B.'s houses and shall get the money together in time to pay, though the money and completion are delayed at first.
